label: rem:bk-coordination-multiplicity
title: The light-nucleus binding multiplicity is the coordination number of $\mathcal{B}_K$
html:
Remark. The light-nucleus binding multiplicity is the coordination number of \mathcal{B}_K

The many-body binding weight of the jet-order filtration factorises as w_n(K) = M_n(A)\,\mathrm{Vol}_n(K), where \mathrm{Vol}_n(K) is the hyperbolic volume of the n-body sub-link of the building-block link \mathcal{B}_K and M_n(A) is a body-order multiplicity. The volume factor is the isospin (T_3) carrier — the {}^3\mathrm{H}/{}^3\mathrm{He} mirror split is supplied by \mathrm{Vol}({}^3\mathrm{H}) > \mathrm{Vol}({}^3\mathrm{He}) with no fit — while the multiplicity M_n(A) was left open. The crossing/coordination structure of \mathcal{B}_K supplies a topological reading of M_n(A).

The multiplicity read off the crossing/coordination structure

Write the per-nucleon coordination number z(A) = A-1 (the number of nucleon–nucleon bonds incident to one nucleon in the fully coordinated cluster) and the total bond count C(A,2) = \tfrac{1}{2}A(A-1). Reading the required multiplicity straight off the AME2020 binding energies, M_{\mathrm{need}}(A) = B_{\mathrm{AME}} / (m_e\,\mathrm{Vol}_A):

isotope \mathcal{B}_K M_{\mathrm{need}} z = A-1
{}^3\mathrm{H} 8_{11} 2.003 2
{}^3\mathrm{He} \mathrm{L6a4} (Borromean) 2.061 2
{}^4\mathrm{He} \mathrm{L6a4} base 7.557 3

For the non-magic A=3 pair the multiplicity is the per-nucleon coordination number z = A-1 = 2, matched to better than 3\% with no free parameter. The doubly-magic {}^4\mathrm{He} requires an additional factor M_{\mathrm{need}}/z = 2.5189, which is close to the super-exponential Schur–Weyl period a_D^{(4)} = \sum_{\lambda \vdash 4} \dim_q \lambda / 4 = 2.5328.

That period is derived, not read off the data: it is a q-dimension sum at the substrate q_0 with no calibration and no free parameter, and its q = 1 limit is the exact rational I(4)/4 = 5/2 with I the involution numbers. The law M(A) = z(A)\,a_D^{(A)} is therefore fixed a priori and can be tested on every point. Tested, it fails: it over-shoots {}^3\mathrm{H} by 33.5\% and {}^3\mathrm{He} by 29.7\% — the \approx 30\% overshoot is this same law refuted one value of A down — and at {}^4\mathrm{He} it lands 0.55\% high, giving B({}^4\mathrm{He}) \approx 28.4517 MeV against the AME2020 value 28.2957 MeV. Since every input to M_{\mathrm{need}} is known to better than one part in 10^{7}, that 0.55\% is a discrepancy rather than an agreement within errors.

Restricting the factor to the magic shell is accordingly a selection between two parameter-free candidates rather than a derivation, and {}^4\mathrm{He} is the only nucleus in the volume-covered range A \le 4 that selects it. A window of width 0.028 about 2.5189 contains further parameter-free candidates, several of them closer than a_D^{(4)}, so the near-match does not single that period out. The Wigner-\mathrm{SU}(4) closed-shell structure cannot supply the factor either: the "at most four rows" restriction is satisfied by every partition of every n \le 4, so it leaves every Schur–Weyl sum below n = 5 unchanged and takes the same value at A = 3 and A = 4 (QOU.Mass.WignerSU4RowBoundInactive).

The deuteron sits on the Seifert-fibred Hopf link, where \mathrm{Vol} = 0 and any volume product vanishes. The crossing structure survives there — the Hopf link has crossing number 2, linking number |\mathrm{lk}| = 1, and per-nucleon coordination z = 1 — so the coordination carrier is the natural non-vanishing replacement for the volume on the two-body sub-link.

That the carrier is a coordination count and not a Gauss linking number is now proved rather than posited (the Brunnian binding channel). The {}^3\mathrm{He} and {}^4\mathrm{He} carriers are Borromean, hence Brunnian: every pairwise linking number vanishes, so a linking-number multiplier would read zero for exactly these nuclei. In the proved crossing-energy channel split the signed (linking-number) channel is empty for a Brunnian pair and the binding is carried by the sign-blind coordination-count channel, which is bar-odd and therefore complementary to the bar-even mass self-weight \mathrm{lw}. The deuteron Hopf case (\mathrm{lk} = z = 1) is the boundary where the two invariants coincide; they diverge at A \geq 3, where only the coordination count is non-vanishing.

Extension: \alpha-cluster coordination for A > 4

The heavier magic nuclei {}^{16}\mathrm{O} and {}^{40}\mathrm{Ca} are not single hyperbolic links but \alpha-conjugate clusters. The coordination principle lifts one level: treating each {}^4\mathrm{He} as one node and counting \alpha–\alpha coordination bonds,

  B(n_\alpha) \approx n_\alpha\,B({}^4\mathrm{He}) + N_{\mathrm{bonds}}\,b_{\alpha\alpha}.

For a simplex cluster (n_\alpha \le 4, complete \alpha-graph realisable up to the tetrahedron) N_{\mathrm{bonds}} = C(n_\alpha, 2), and the residual per bond is a near-constant b_{\alpha\alpha} \approx 2.41\,\text{MeV} ({}^{12}\mathrm{C}: 2.425; {}^{16}\mathrm{O}: 2.406). These per-bond b_{\alpha\alpha} values are empirical near-constants read off the AME data (not derived — the same data-selected \alpha-\alpha coefficient honestly labelled in rem:alpha-cluster-model-g-closure). The closed-shell factor M_{\mathrm{need}}/z = 2.5189 is likewise an AME read; the Schur–Weyl period a_D^{(4)} = 2.5328 it is compared against is derived, but the identification of the two is not, as recorded above. The single \alpha–\alpha pair {}^8\mathrm{Be} gives \approx 0, consistent with its being unbound relative to two \alpha-particles. For n_\alpha \ge 5 the complete graph over-counts — not all pairs can be nearest neighbours in three dimensions — and the per-bond residual falls, so the coordination number saturates to a geometric close-packing count. That count is bounded by the three-dimensional kissing number 12: the touching pairs in any packing of n unit balls in \mathbb{E}^3 number fewer than 6n - 0.926\,n^{2/3} [bezdek-reid2013] (Thm.~1(i)), an affine bulk 12 \cdot n/2 minus a sub-affine surface deficit; the density statement behind the fcc picture is the Kepler theorem [hales-etal2010], which itself proves no contact bound. This reproduces the classical Hafstad–Teller \alpha-bond picture with N_{\mathrm{bonds}} read as the \alpha-cluster coordination number, the same principle as z = A-1 one level up.
